Q: payPal subscription transactions not showing up immediately A:

The first subscription payment is sometimes delayed.

Move the first payment to setup fee and shift the beginning of the subscription to the next billing cycle. The setup fee is credited immediately. With `setupFeeFailureAction: 'CANCEL',` the subscription not start if the setup fee doesn't go through. This way there's no need to use IPN or webhooks to find out if a subscription successfully started.

Q: TensorFlow 2.0 - AttributeError: module 'tensorflow' has no attribute 'Session' A:

TensorFlow v2.0 supports Eager mode vis-à-vis Graph mode of v1.0.

Hence, tf.session() is not supported on v2.0. Hence, I would suggest you to rewrite your code to work in Eager mode.

Q: Why does order of 3 loops in Floyd-Warshall matters? A:

Floyd Warshall is a type of DP. Its transition is dp[i][j] = dp[i][k] + dp[k][j]

You cannot build upon the result of a k until all the paths through this k are finalized.

For example we want to find distance from A to D:
A → B = 1
B → C = 1
C → D = 1
A → D = 1000

If you have k in the innerloop, then you might start with i = A, j = D, then you try B and C as different k, but at this point we have not visited the paths through B or C, so you end up with A → D = 1000

Yes, later you will hit combination i = B, j = D, k = C, now C as k are initialized. But you are never going back to i = A, j = D to fix its distance with C

Instead if you have k in the outerloop, no matter what order you visited the k, you have tried all combination of i & j before moving on to the next k, so that's fine

  • If you pick k = B first, you have dp[A][C] = 2, so later k = C can build upon k = B: dp[A][D] = dp[A][C] + dp[C][D] = 2 + 1 = 3

  • if you pick k = C first, you have dp[B][D] = 2, so later k = B can build upon it: dp[A][D] = dp[A][B] + dp[B][D] = 1 + 2 = 3

Q: InfiniBand explained A:

InfiniBand is a high-performance interconnect mainly used in HPC and AI clusters. Compared with Ethernet, it is designed from the ground up for low latency, high throughput, and lossless RDMA communication, rather than general-purpose networking.

“Switch-based interconnect” means InfiniBand uses a switched fabric topology: all nodes are connected through switches using point-to-point links, not a shared medium. When multiple inputs target the same output, there are no collisions — traffic is handled by hardware scheduling and credit-based flow control inside the switches.

The end-to-end flow control means a sender only transmits when the receiver has available buffer credits, so packet loss and retransmissions are avoided. Because this mechanism is built into the fabric, InfiniBand does not rely on complex in-network congestion control like Ethernet (PFC/ECN), which is one of the reasons it achieves lower and more predictable latency.

A clear comparison can be found here:https://www.naddod.com/blog/differences-between-infiniband-and-ethernet-networks

Q: undefined reference to omp_get_thread_num using OpenMP and cmake? A:

Maybe I'm a little bit late to the question. However, I've encountered the same problem recently.

It was resolved by purging the tbb package on my linux os.

The theory is that the tbb package conflicts with the OpenMP, and it won't show up at the stage of compilation.

Specifically, I removed the libtbb-dev package with

sudo apt remove libtbb-dev

as described here,

https://github.com/caiowakamatsu/CRender/blob/master/readme.md
